pageCache.pageTitle: Virtues & Mission - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our mission and virtues
At St Catharine’s, our vision is shaped by the life and witness of St Catharine of Alexandria, a saint known for her deep faith, wisdom and extraordinary courage. Her example inspires us to be learners who seek truth, uphold justice and treat every person with dignity and kindness.
St Catharine’s Primary School provides an inclusive Catholic education, expressing love of and trust in Jesus. We empower individuals to “Let Their Light Shine” through courage, compassion and community.
We believe that every child is created in the image of God and has unique gifts to offer the world. In line with Catholic Social Teaching, we place the dignity of the human person, the call to community, and our responsibility to care for one another at the heart of school life. Through prayer, learning and service, we help our pupils grow into thoughtful, confident and loving individuals who can make a positive difference to society.
Our virtues
Developed with pupils, parents, staff, governors and our parish family, our three virtues represent the kind of people we want our children to become, now and in the future. They guide our relationships, our behaviour and the way we approach learning every day.
Courage
Following the example of St Catharine, who stood bravely for her beliefs, we help children face challenges with confidence, honesty and resilience. Courage allows pupils to take responsible risks, try new ideas and stand up for what is right.
Human DignitySolidarity
“Be strong and courageous… for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Compassion
Compassion teaches us to understand, forgive and care deeply for one another. Inspired by Christ’s unconditional love, we nurture empathy in every child, helping them to notice the needs of others and respond with kindness.
Option for the Poor and VulnerableRights and Responsibilities
“Be kind and compassionate to one another…”
Community
St Paul reminds us that we are one body in Christ, each with a unique part to play. Our school celebrates this by encouraging belonging, cooperation and responsibility, helping pupils recognise their role in building a fair, inclusive and joyful school.
ParticipationThe Common Good
“The body is one and has many members… so it is with Christ.”
Our school prayer
Dear Heavenly Father, Friend of all the children, bless us all at St Catharine’s School. Bless the pupils, teachers and everyone who works here. Help us all to do our best. Help us to be kind to one another and to be cheerful throughout the day. Amen

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
All schools in England must actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs, both in lessons and beyond the classroom.
At St Catharine’s, these values are woven into everyday school life and sit naturally alongside our Gospel values.
Our Gospel values
As a Catholic primary school, we also uphold the values of the Gospel: love and compassion, forgiveness and mercy, humility and dignity, respect for all, justice and peace.
Guided by our motto, “Let your light shine”, we strive to be a community where everyone is equally respected and unconditionally loved.
How we promote British values
Democracy
Adults listen to pupils’ views and value their opinions, and children learn to listen to and respect the views of others, supported by our oracy work. Pupils elect their own School Parliament, whose members gather the views of their classmates. This helps children understand how democracy gives everyone a voice. Our children have visited Parliament, one pupil was invited to speak there about saving bees, and pupils have written to the Prime Minister about climate change.
In action:School Parliament electionsOracyPupil voice
The rule of law
The importance of rules and laws is reinforced in class and in assemblies. Children learn that laws protect us, that they bring responsibilities, and that there are consequences when they are broken. Everyone follows our three school rules, Ready, Respectful, Safe. Visits to Skillzone and from local community representatives reinforce these messages. Children learn that we are all equal under the law, and that discriminating against others because of characteristics such as age, disability, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation is not only wrong but illegal.
In action:Ready, Respectful, SafeSkillzoneCommunity visitors
Individual liberty
Pupils are encouraged to be independent learners who make choices within a safe and supportive environment. We help children build their self-esteem and confidence, and to understand their personal freedoms and how to use them well. Through RE and PSHE, children learn consideration for others, and they enthusiastically support local, national and global charities. Online safety teaching helps them make safe choices online.
In action:PSHECharity workOnline safety
Mutual respect
Assemblies promote respect for others and the importance of good manners. Children learn the value of self-respect, honesty, open communication and fair play. Pupils work together, listen to each other and value one another’s opinions.
In action:AssembliesCollaborative learningFair play
Tolerance of different faiths and beliefs
As a Catholic worshipping community, we help pupils understand their place in a culturally diverse society through RE and the spiritual life of the school. Assemblies and class work celebrate diversity and every person’s right to be respected and valued equally, whatever their faith or belief. We have no outsiders and we extend a welcome to all. We believe this welcome goes further than tolerance.
In action:Religious EducationCollective WorshipNo outsiders

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Catharine’s
I would like to warmly welcome you to our website. It is a privilege to be the headteacher of this school, and I would like to share with you what underpins our work here.
St Catharine’s Catholic Primary School is a family based on the love of God and each other. All children are precious and unique, and the special talents that each person brings to St Catharine’s are celebrated, in partnership with home, parish and the wider community. St Catharine’s provides a happy, secure learning environment and a rich curriculum, through which all children are encouraged to “be more” and to strive to make a difference.
Our staff, governors and parents work together to nurture self-confident young people who proudly celebrate all the things that make them unique. This is why our school motto is central to our whole ethos: we encourage our pupils to “Let your light shine” every day, helping them to fulfil their potential and make the most of their talents.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Social Teaching - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
The principles of Catholic Social Teaching underpin every aspect of life at St Catharine’s. Rooted in the example of St Catharine of Alexandria, we strive to live out the Gospel with courage, compassion and a deep sense of community. Our faith calls us to love God and to love our neighbour, especially those experiencing poverty, injustice or exclusion.
Catholic Social Teaching is grounded in the life and words of Jesus Christ. Pope Francis reminded us that Catholic schools should help young people put their faith into loving, meaningful action, so that it shapes not only their own lives but also transforms society for the better.
Guided by our virtues
Our virtues help children understand how to live their faith authentically and responsibly in today’s world.
The themes of Catholic Social Teaching
Human Dignity
Every person is created in the image of God. All lives are precious, and every child at St Catharine’s is taught to respect and value the dignity of others in all that they say and do.
Option for the Poor and Vulnerable
We are called to put the needs of the poor and vulnerable first. Children are encouraged to notice those in need and respond with kindness, service and compassion, living out Christ’s call to care for the marginalised.
Participation
Every child is encouraged to take an active role in school life. From classroom discussions and assemblies to liturgies and charitable projects, pupils learn that their voice and actions can make a difference.
Rights and Responsibilities
Every person has fundamental rights, including food, education, healthcare and shelter. Children learn that these rights come with responsibilities: to respect the rights of others and contribute positively to their community.
Solidarity
We are all part of God’s family. Children learn that what happens to one person affects everyone, locally, nationally and globally. Through service, awareness projects and acts of kindness, we build a culture of unity and support.
Stewardship of Creation
God has entrusted the world to us. Pupils care for creation through eco-projects, outdoor learning and everyday acts of responsibility, so that future generations can enjoy and benefit from the world we share.
Subsidiarity
Decisions should be made as closely as possible to those affected by them. Children learn to take responsibility for themselves, support each other, and understand that everyone has a role to play in solving problems fairly and thoughtfully.
The Common Good
Our community works together so that everyone can thrive. Children are taught to consider the wellbeing of others, to act with justice, and to help build a school and world that is fair, peaceful and welcoming for everyone.
“It is our moral compass, guiding us on how to live out our faith in the world.”
Catholic Social Teaching is an integral part of our identity. It shapes our curriculum, influences our decisions and inspires our pupils to “Let Their Light Shine” as people of courage, compassion and community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Patron Saint - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our patron saint: St Catharine of Alexandria
Our school is named after St Catharine of Alexandria, one of the Church’s most inspiring early Christian witnesses. Her story has shaped our identity as a school and continues to guide our mission, virtues and daily life together.
Her story
Wisdom
Born in the late 3rd century, St Catharine was known for her remarkable intelligence, strong faith and deep sense of justice.
Courage
Tradition tells us that she challenged the powerful with wisdom far beyond her years, speaking courageously in defence of Christian truth and remaining steadfast in her love for Christ.
Faith
When she refused to abandon her faith, she was imprisoned and eventually martyred. Those who met her saw not fear, but extraordinary compassion and strength.
Our virtues
St Catharine’s qualities shape our three core virtues, chosen with our pupils, families and staff.
In following her example, we encourage our children to seek truth, stand up for what is right, show kindness to all, and recognise the dignity of every person, reflecting the principles of Catholic Social Teaching in our everyday actions.
St Catharine’s Day: 25 November
Each year we celebrate our patron saint’s feast day with a special Mass in our church with the parish community, followed by celebrations in school.
Here’s how we celebrated in 2025.
View this post on Instagram
Our links with the parish
Our connection to St Catharine’s Church is an important part of our community life and plays a central role in the spiritual formation of our pupils. We work closely with the parish priest and parish community to help children grow in their relationship with God and understand their place within the wider Church family. This partnership enriches the prayer life of the school and gives our pupils regular, meaningful encounters with faith.
Celebrating Mass together
Our children gather regularly at St Catharine’s Church for Mass, at key points in the liturgical year and for special school celebrations.
Children are encouraged to take active roles as readers, musicians and singers, helping them grow in confidence, leadership and ownership of their faith.
Preparing for the sacraments
We work closely with the parish to support children preparing for the sacraments.
How school supports the parish programme Sacramental programmes are led by the parish. The school plays an essential supporting role by:
✓providing dedicated learning time and resources

pageCache.pageTitle: English: Reading - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Supporting Information
At St Catharine’s, reading lies at the heart of our curriculum and our school community. It underpins all areas of learning and is central to pupils’ academic success, personal development and future opportunities.
We are committed to ensuring that every child becomes a fluent, confident and motivated reader. Our approach is equitable and inclusive: we provide high-quality, research-informed universal provision alongside carefully targeted academic support for pupils at risk of underachievement.
Our reading strategy is rooted in evidence, particularly guidance from the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF). We prioritise:
We believe that all children can learn to read with the right teaching and support, and that fostering a love of reading is essential to lifelong success.
Reading Implementation
We believe that developing a lifelong love of reading is fundamental to pupils’ success and wellbeing. Reading is promoted across the curriculum through exposure to high-quality, carefully selected texts.
Across EYFS, KS1 and KS2, pupils engage with a wide range of literature, including fiction, non-fiction and poetry. Texts are chosen to reflect our curriculum, broaden pupils’ cultural capital and promote discussion and critical thinking.
Teaching reflects EEF guidance through:
Developing Early Reading
Universal Provision for Word Reading
In EYFS and Key Stage 1, we teach reading through the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised programme, supported by our work with the English Hub.
Pupils are taught to:
Phonics is taught daily at a brisk pace using the structure: revisit, teach, practise and apply. Teaching is systematic and carefully sequenced to build on prior learning and secure progress.
Children read fully decodable books matched to their phonic knowledge as early as possible. This ensures they can confidently decode texts, allowing cognitive resources to focus on comprehension.
Phonics teaching is embedded within a rich curriculum that develops speaking and listening, language acquisition and early reading for pleasure.
Targeted Academic Support for Word Reading
Assessment is integral to our phonics provision. Staff routinely assess pupils’ recognition of phonemes, as well as their ability to blend and segment.
Pupils who require additional support receive timely Keep-Up or Catch-Up interventions, closely matched to need. These may include additional practice, small group work or one-to-one support.
This ensures that all pupils keep up with the programme and make strong progress.
Universal Approach for Comprehension
From Year 2 to Year 6, pupils take part in regular whole-class reading sessions, designed to develop fluency, comprehension and vocabulary. In Years 2 and 3, pupils build reading fluency through Little Wandle Fluency, focusing on accuracy, automaticity and prosody. In Years 4 and 5, this progression continues through Project X, supporting pupils to refine fluency and deepen comprehension.
Whole-class reading sessions:
This approach aligns with EEF guidance by combining explicit strategy instruction with high-quality discussion and modelling.
Assessment is used effectively to inform teaching and identify next steps.
We use a combination of:
Assessment is regular, purposeful and aligned with EEF recommendations, ensuring gaps are identified and addressed quickly.
Reading for Pleasure in School
Reading for pleasure is prioritised across the school. Pupils are read to daily and engage in regular book talk.
We promote reading through:
Enrichment opportunities include:
Reading for Pleasure at Home
We work in partnership with families to promote reading beyond school.
We support parents through guidance, workshops and reading initiatives, recognising the importance of home reading in developing fluency and enjoyment.
Our Core Aim for Pupils
Our core aim is for all pupils to become fluent, confident and enthusiastic readers.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will:
We aim for pupils to leave St Catharine’s as reflective, curious and motivated readers who read widely for both pleasure and purpose, fully prepared for the next stage of their education.

pageCache.pageTitle: French - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
French Vision 2026/27
Our Approach to Teaching French
French is taught across years 3 to 6, using the Language Angels scheme to ensure a consistent, engaging and progressive approach to language learning. Lessons are carefully sequenced to develop pupils’ listening, speaking, reading and writing skills, with regular opportunities to revisit and build upon prior learning.
Teaching is interactive and inclusive, using songs, games and structured speaking activities to build confidence, accurate pronunciation and enjoyment. Language Angels’ assessment tools support teachers in monitoring progress and meeting the needs of all learners. Cultural learning is woven throughout lessons, helping pupils to develop curiosity and respect for other cultures.
French has been chosen as our modern foreign language because Chipping Campden is twinned with Pont-d’Ouilly in France, giving pupils a meaningful and relevant context for their language learning and strengthening links with the wider community.
Our Core Aim for Pupils
Our core aim is for pupils to develop a secure foundation in French and a positive attitude towards language learning. By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will be able to communicate using simple spoken and written French, demonstrate accurate pronunciation, and show an understanding of French culture.
We aim for pupils to leave primary school as confident, curious and motivated language learners, well prepared for further study and aware of the value of learning languages in an increasingly connected world.

pageCache.text:
Supporting Information
PSHE and RHE Vision 2026 – 2027
Our Approach to PSHE and RHE
At St Catharine’s School, PSHE and RHE is central to our mission to develop valued individuals who are equipped to live healthy, fulfilled lives and contribute positively to God’s world. PSHE and RHE is taught through TenTen Resources, Life to the Full Plus scheme of Catholic PSHE and RSE, A spiral curriculum designed in line with the National Curriculum and adapted to include the 2025 DfE statutory guidance for Relationships Education and Health Education and informed by the PSHE and RHE Association Programme of Study.
Each class operates as a community of citizens, where children learn to respect themselves and others, recognise human dignity, and develop the skills needed to thrive academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually. Learning takes place in a safe, inclusive and respectful environment, where discussion, reflection and empathy are encouraged.
PSHE and RHE is delivered through discrete, planned lessons across the year, alongside opportunities for learning to be revisited and applied across the wider curriculum, particularly in Science, Computing and RE. The school follows the TenTen Diocesan-approved Relationships and Sex Education programme, supplemented by input from Gloucestershire Police’s School beat officer in upper Key Stage 2 and ensuring comprehensive coverage of wellbeing, online safety and healthy lifestyles. Content is taught through rolling programmes to ensure progression and age-appropriate learning.
Teaching is inclusive and responsive to need, with appropriate support and challenge for all learners, including pupils with SEND. Learning is enhanced through national initiatives, external visitors and real-life experiences. Assessment is ongoing and proportionate, using formative feedback, summative reporting and pupil voice to ensure the curriculum has a positive impact on wellbeing and personal development.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Governance at St Catharine’s
St Catharine’s is part of the Little Way Catholic Educational Trust (LWCET). The Trust is governed by a Board of Directors, who are responsible for the management and administration of the Trust and all of its academies.
The Board’s constitution and rules are set out in the Trust’s Memorandum and Articles of Association. The Directors have overall responsibility and final decision-making authority for all of the Trust’s work. They are accountable to the Charity Commission, the Department for Education and the Education & Skills Funding Agency (or any successor bodies), as well as to the Bishop of Clifton.
Read the LWCET Register of Interests
Meet the Governors 2026–27
Our Local Governing Committee
The Directors appoint a Local Governing Committee (LGC) for each academy. The LGC is a group of volunteers, known as governors. The Directors decide how each LGC is made up and how it runs. The Scheme of Delegation sets this out and describes the authority the Directors give the LGC to run the academy and fulfil its mission.
The LGC holds the Headteacher to account for:
Some of this work happens in smaller committees, which then report back to the full LGC. Each governor acts as a “critical friend”. They celebrate the school’s achievements and also point out where it could improve, so that support and challenge stay in balance. Governors also check progress towards our strategic priorities and make sure policies are put into practice correctly.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - St Catharine's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music Vision 2025/26
Our Approach to Teaching Music
Music is taught across EYFS, KS1 and KS2 using the Charanga scheme, which is aligned with the National Curriculum and Model Music Curriculum. Lessons are carefully sequenced to ensure progression in knowledge and skills, enabling pupils to develop as musicians over time.
Pupils learn through singing, listening, composing and performing, while developing an understanding of the inter-related dimensions of music, including pulse, pitch, tempo, dynamics, timbre, texture and structure. Music is taught as a practical and creative subject, where each class becomes a community of musicians.
Singing is central to our music provision. Pupils sing regularly in lessons, collective worship and weekly singing assemblies led by specialist musicians. Performance opportunities are embedded throughout the school year, including liturgies, productions and community events, giving pupils a sense of purpose and audience.
Additional to our curriculum, pupils also have opportunities to learn instruments, including whole-class ensemble brass teaching in Key Stage 2, alongside access to peripatetic music lessons. Our strong links with local organisations and the wider community enrich pupils’ musical experiences and expose them to a wide range of musical styles and traditions.
Our Core Aim for Pupils
Our core aim is for pupils to develop confidence, creativity and a lifelong love of music.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will be able to perform, compose and listen with increasing accuracy, fluency and expression. They will understand key musical concepts, use appropriate vocabulary and appreciate a range of musical styles and traditions.
We aim for pupils to leave St Catharine’s as confident performers and reflective listeners who value music as a form of expression, creativity and community, and who are well prepared to continue their musical journey beyond primary school.
